questions.question: Vidhya lent Rs. 6000 to Kavya for 3 years at the rate of 4% per annum compound interest. Calculate the amount that Vidhya will get after 3 years.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective Compound Interest rate for 3 years at r% is calculated as: 3r . 3r² . r³

For r = 4%, Effective Rate = 3(4) . 3(16) . (64) = 12.4864%

Total Amount = Principal + Interest = 100% + 12.4864% = 112.4864%

Amount = 112.4864% of 6000 = 6749.184 ≈ 6749.18

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 6749.18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Principal (P) = Rs. 6000

⇒ Rate (R) = 4% per annum

⇒ Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

questions.question: Which of the following statement is TRUE for Whole Numbers?

options.text: They include zero and positive integers.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Whole numbers are simply the set of natural numbers (counting numbers) along with zero.

Set of Whole Numbers (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...}

This means they include zero and all positive integers, but no fractions or negative numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is They include zero and positive integers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Checking all the given statements:**

⇒ Option 1: They include fractions. (False, fractions like 1/2 or 3/4 are Rational Numbers, not Whole Numbers)

⇒ Option 2: They include negative numbers. (False, negative numbers like −1 or −5 belong to Integers, not Whole Numbers)

⇒ Option 4: They start from 1. (False, numbers starting from 1 are called Natural Numbers)

⇒ Option 3: They include zero and positive integers. (True)

**Derivation:**

⇒ The set of Whole Numbers is mathematically denoted by W.

⇒ W = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...}

⇒ The numbers {1, 2, 3, 4, ...} are positive integers.

⇒ Therefore, Whole Numbers = {0} + Positive Integers.

**∴ The correct answer is They include zero and positive integers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers (N)

These are the counting numbers starting from 1. N = {1, 2, 3, 4, ...}. They do not include zero, negative numbers, or fractions.

Integers (Z)

This set includes all whole numbers and their negative counterparts. Z = {..., −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.

Rational Numbers (Q)

Any number that can be expressed in the form of p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not equal to zero. It includes fractions, terminating decimals, and repeating decimals.

Real Numbers (R)

The set of all rational and irrational numbers. They represent all possible continuous points on the number line.

questions.question: Dhiraj goes to his school from his house at a speed of 3.8 km/hr and returns at 2.6 km/ hr. If he takes 5 hours going and coming, the distance between his house and school is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When total time (T) to travel a distance (D) back and forth with speeds S₁ and S₂ is given, use the direct formula:

D = T × (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

D = 5 × (3.8 × 2.6) ÷ (3.8 + 2.6)

D = 5 × 9.88 ÷ 6.4 = 7.71875 ≈ 7.72 km

**∴ The correct answer is 7.72 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed going to school (v₁) = 3.8 km/hr

Speed returning from school (v₂) = 2.6 km/hr

Total time taken (T) = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Time = (Distance ÷ v₁) + (Distance ÷ v₂)

 
 House 
 School 
• Distance = D 
• 
 3.8 km/hr 
• 
 2.6 km/hr Total Time = 5 hours 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance between his house and school be D km.

⇒ Total time = Time taken to go + Time taken to return

⇒ (D ÷ 3.8) + (D ÷ 2.6) = 5

⇒ D × [(1 ÷ 3.8) + (1 ÷ 2.6)] = 5

⇒ D × [(2.6 + 3.8) ÷ (3.8 × 2.6)] = 5

⇒ D × (6.4 ÷ 9.88) = 5

⇒ D = (5 × 9.88) ÷ 6.4

⇒ D = 49.4 ÷ 6.4

⇒ D = 7.71875 km

⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, we get D ≈ 7.72 km

**∴ The correct answer is 7.72 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When a person travels equal distances at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the complete journey is calculated using the formula: Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Distance from Difference in Time

If instead of total time, the difference in time (ΔT) taken to cover a distance D at speeds S₁ and S₂ is given, the distance is: D = ΔT × (S₁ × S₂) ÷ |S₁ − S₂|.

Relative Speed

When two entities travel in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If they travel in the same direction, it becomes the difference of their speeds (S₁ − S₂).

questions.question: A spherical shell has an outer diameter of 20 cm and is 1 cm thick. What is the volume of the material in the shell? (Use π=3.14).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Outer radius (R) = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm, Inner radius (r) = 10 − 1 = 9 cm.

Volume of spherical shell = (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)

Volume = (4/3) × 3.14 × (10³ − 9³) = (4/3) × 3.14 × (1000 − 729)

Volume = (4/3) × 3.14 × 271 = 3403.76 ÷ 3 ≈ 1134.6 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1134.6 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outer diameter of the spherical shell = 20 cm

Thickness of the shell = 1 cm

Value of π = 3.14

 
• r = 9 cm 
• R = 10 cm 
• Thickness = 1 cm Cross-section of the Spherical Shell 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a spherical shell = (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)

Where R = Outer radius and r = Inner radius

**Calculations:**

⇒ Outer radius (R) = Outer diameter ÷ 2 = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm

⇒ Inner radius (r) = Outer radius − Thickness = 10 − 1 = 9 cm

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × 3.14 × (10³ − 9³)

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × 3.14 × (1000 − 729)

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × 3.14 × 271

⇒ Volume = 3403.76 ÷ 3

⇒ Volume = 1134.586... ≈ 1134.6 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1134.6 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Solid Sphere

The volume of a solid sphere of radius r is given by V = (4/3) × π × r³.

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a solid sphere of radius r is given by A = 4 × π × r².

Volume of a Hemisphere

The volume of a solid hemisphere of radius r is exactly half of a full sphere: V = (2/3) × π × r³.

Total Surface Area of a Hemispherical Shell

For a hemispherical shell with outer radius R and inner radius r, the total surface area = 3 × π × R² + π × r².

questions.question: A rectangular aquarium (100 cm L × 50 cm W × 60 cm H) contains water with an initial level of 20 cm. 10 identical metal spheres, each with a diameter of 10 cm, are gently lowered into the aquarium. Assuming the spheres are fully submerged, what is the rise in the water level?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rise in water level = (Total Volume of submerged objects) ÷ (Base Area of the container)

Rise in level = [10 × (4/3) × π × 5³] ÷ (100 × 50)

Rise in level = (5000π / 3) ÷ 5000

Rise in level = π/3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is π/3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Aquarium length (L) = 100 cm, width (W) = 50 cm

⇒ Number of metal spheres (n) = 10

⇒ Diameter of each sphere = 10 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ Displaced Volume = Base Area of container × Rise in fluid level

 
 
• 
• 
• 20 cm 
• 
• Rise: h Base Area = 100 × 50 = 5000 cm² 
• 10 Spheres r = 5 cm Volume Displaced = Total Volume of Spheres 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Base area of the aquarium = 100 × 50 = 5000 cm²

⇒ Volume of one sphere = (4/3) × π × 5³ = 500π / 3 cm³

⇒ Total volume of 10 spheres = 10 × (500π / 3) = 5000π / 3 cm³

⇒ Let the rise in water level be h cm.

⇒ Volume of water displaced = Total volume of the fully submerged spheres

⇒ Base Area × h = 5000π / 3

⇒ 5000 × h = 5000π / 3

⇒ h = π / 3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is π/3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Archimedes' Principle (Submerged Volume)

When solid objects are completely submerged in a liquid, the volume of liquid displaced is exactly equal to the total volume of the submerged objects.

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a sphere is given by V = (4÷3) × π × r³, where r is the radius of the sphere.

Rise in Liquid Level

The rise in the fluid level (h) in any container with a uniform vertical cross-section can be calculated directly by the relation: h = (Total Volume of submerged objects) ÷ (Base Area).

questions.question: A', 'B', and 'C' formed a consulting firm. Their capital investments were Rs. 6,00,000, Rs. 4,00,000, and Rs. 5,00,000, respectively. After 3 months, 'A' withdrew Rs. 1,00,000, and 'B' added Rs. 1,00,000. The partnership lasted for 9 months. What was the ratio of their effective capital contributions?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Capital = Capital × Time

A's effective capital = (6 × 3) + (5 × 6) = 18 + 30 = 48

B's effective capital = (4 × 3) + (5 × 6) = 12 + 30 = 42

C's effective capital = 5 × 9 = 45

Ratio = 48 : 42 : 45 = 16 : 14 : 15

**∴ The correct answer is 16:14:15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial investments: A = Rs. 6,00,000, B = Rs. 4,00,000, C = Rs. 5,00,000

After 3 months: A withdrew Rs. 1,00,000; B added Rs. 1,00,000

Total time of partnership = 9 months

**Formula Used:**

Ratio of Profit = Ratio of Effective Capital = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂) : (C₃ × T₃)

 A 6L × 3m 5L × 6m B 4L × 3m 5L × 6m C 5L × 9m 
• 0 3 Months 9 Months 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A's investment for first 3 months = Rs. 6,00,000

⇒ A's investment for remaining 6 months = 6,00,000 − 1,00,000 = Rs. 5,00,000

⇒ A's effective capital = (6,00,000 × 3) + (5,00,000 × 6) = 18,00,000 + 30,00,000 = Rs. 48,00,000

 

⇒ B's investment for first 3 months = Rs. 4,00,000

⇒ B's investment for remaining 6 months = 4,00,000 + 1,00,000 = Rs. 5,00,000

⇒ B's effective capital = (4,00,000 × 3) + (5,00,000 × 6) = 12,00,000 + 30,00,000 = Rs. 42,00,000

 

⇒ C's investment for entire 9 months = Rs. 5,00,000

⇒ C's effective capital = 5,00,000 × 9 = Rs. 45,00,000

 

⇒ Ratio of their effective capitals = 48,00,000 : 42,00,000 : 45,00,000

⇒ Canceling 1,00,000 from all terms, Ratio = 48 : 42 : 45

⇒ Dividing by 3, Ratio = 16 : 14 : 15

**∴ The correct answer is 16:14:15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When all partners invest their capital for the exact same period, profits are distributed strictly in the ratio of their original investments.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different time periods, profits are distributed in the ratio of their effective capitals (calculated as Capital × Time).

Active and Sleeping Partners

An active partner receives a fixed salary or a certain percentage of total profit for managing the business operations, while the remaining profit is shared among all partners according to their effective capital ratios.

questions.question: The price of a product is decreased by x% and then increased by x%. The final price becomes 10% less than the original. What is the value of x (approximately)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a value is first decreased by x% and then increased by x%, the net change is always a decrease of (x² ÷ 100)%.

Given the net decrease is 10%:

⇒ x² ÷ 100 = 10

⇒ x² = 1000

⇒ x = √1000 ≈ 31.62

**∴ The correct answer is 31.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial decrease in price = x%

Subsequent increase in price = x%

Final price is 10% less than the original price.

**Formula Used:**

Net percentage change for successive changes a% and b% = (a + b + a × b ÷ 100)%

**Calculation:**

 Original Price 100 
• 
 − x% Intermediate Decreased 
• 
 + x% Final Price 90 
 Net Decrease: 10% 

⇒ Let the original price be 100.

⇒ Since the final price is 10% less, Final Price = 100 − 10 = 90.

⇒ Using the successive percentage formula where a = −x and b = +x:

⇒ Net Change = −x + x + (−x × x) ÷ 100

⇒ Net Change = −x² ÷ 100

⇒ The negative sign confirms an overall decrease.

⇒ Equating the net decrease to the given 10%:

⇒ x² ÷ 100 = 10

⇒ x² = 1000

⇒ x = √1000 ≈ 31.62

**∴ The correct answer is 31.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: Net Change = (a + b + a × b ÷ 100)%. Use a positive sign for an increase and a negative sign for a decrease.

Equal Increase and Decrease

If a quantity is increased by x% and subsequently decreased by the same x%, or vice versa, the final value is always less than the original. The net percentage decrease is always exactly (x² ÷ 100)%.

Base Value Concept

Any percentage calculation is computed on a reference base value. When multiple percentage changes occur sequentially, the intermediate value immediately becomes the new base for the next percentage calculation.

questions.question: A floor is 12 m by 9 m. If tiles of 1.5 m × 1.5 m are used, how many tiles are needed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of tiles along the length = 12 ÷ 1.5 = 8

Number of tiles along the breadth = 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6

Total number of tiles required = 8 × 6 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48 tiles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the floor (L) = 12 m

Breadth of the floor (B) = 9 m

Side of one square tile (a) = 1.5 m

**Formula Used:**

Number of tiles = Total Area of floor ÷ Area of one tile

Number of tiles = (L × B) ÷ a²

 12 m 9 m 
• Tile: 1.5 m × 1.5 m 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of the floor = 12 × 9 = 108 m²

⇒ Area of one square tile = 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25 m²

⇒ Number of tiles = 108 ÷ 2.25

⇒ Number of tiles = 10800 ÷ 225 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48 tiles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The area of a rectangle is the product of its length and breadth: Area = L × B. Its perimeter is defined as 2 × (L + B).

Area of a Square

The area of a square is the square of its side length: Area = a². Its perimeter is defined as 4 × a.

Tiling Concept

When covering a larger flat area with smaller uniform regular shapes (like tiles), the total number required is always the total area divided by the area of one unit shape.

questions.question: A store sign is a 5 m × 4 m rectangle with a 2 m × 1 m rectangle cut out. Painting cost is ₹180/m². How much will the painting cost for the exposed area?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area of the sign = 5 × 4 = 20 m²

Area of cut-out = 2 × 1 = 2 m²

Exposed area to be painted = 20 − 2 = 18 m²

Total painting cost = 18 × 180 = ₹3,240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 5 m 4 m 2 m 1 m Cut out Exposed Area 

**Given:**

Dimensions of the full store sign = 5 m × 4 m

Dimensions of the cut-out section = 2 m × 1 m

Rate of painting = ₹180 per m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of a Rectangle = Length × Width

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the entire store sign = 5 × 4 = 20 m²

⇒ Area of the rectangular cut-out = 2 × 1 = 2 m²

⇒ Exposed Area = Area of store sign − Area of cut-out

⇒ Exposed Area = 20 − 2 = 18 m²

⇒ Cost of painting = Exposed Area × Rate of painting

⇒ Cost of painting = 18 × 180 = 3240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The space occupied by a 2D rectangle is found by the formula: Area = Length × Width.

Area of Composite Figures

The area of a composite shape having a missing portion (cut-out) is determined by calculating the total area of the primary shape and subtracting the exact area of the removed portion.

Total Cost Calculation

The total cost of painting, paving or fencing a specific region is obtained by multiplying the required area (or perimeter) by the designated unit rate. (Cost = Total Area × Unit Rate).

questions.question: A regular hexagonal nut has outer side 6 cm and inner hollow side 3 cm. What is the material approximate area in the cross-section?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a hollow regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × (Outer Side² − Inner Side²)

⇒ Area = (3 × 1.732 ÷ 2) × (6² − 3²)

⇒ Area = 2.598 × (36 − 9)

⇒ Area = 2.598 × 27 = 70.146 ≈ 70 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 70 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outer side of the hexagonal nut (R) = 6 cm

Inner hollow side of the hexagonal nut (r) = 3 cm

 
 
 
• 
• 
• 6 cm 
• 
• 
• 3 cm Cross-section of Hexagonal Nut 

**Formula Used:**

Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × a²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the outer regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 6²

⇒ Area of outer hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 36 = 54√3 cm²

⇒ Area of the inner hollow regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 3²

⇒ Area of inner hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 9 = 13.5√3 cm²

⇒ Cross-sectional area of the material = Area of outer hexagon − Area of inner hexagon

⇒ Material Area = 54√3 − 13.5√3 = 40.5√3 cm²

⇒ Taking √3 ≈ 1.732, Area = 40.5 × 1.732 = 70.146 cm²

⇒ Rounding to the nearest whole number, Area ≈ 70 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 70 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Regular Hexagon

A regular hexagon can be completely divided into 6 equilateral triangles. The total area is exactly 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × a² = (3√3 ÷ 2) × a², where 'a' is the length of its side.

Inradius of a Regular Hexagon

The radius of the inscribed circle (also called the apothem) is the perpendicular distance from the geometric center to any flat side, given by r = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Circumradius of a Regular Hexagon

The radius of the circumscribed circle passing through all six outer vertices is exactly equal to the side length of the regular hexagon, therefore R = a.

questions.question: A man got 10% of his investment as profit. If he invested Rs. 5000, and the profit was reinvested, what will be the total value after the second year with the same profit rate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Reinvesting the profit is equivalent to calculating Compound Interest.

Effective interest rate for 2 successive years at 10% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 21%.

Total value after 2 years will be 121% of the initial investment.

Total Value = (121 ÷ 100) × 5000 = 121 × 50 = 6050.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 6050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Investment (P) = Rs. 5000

Profit Rate (R) = 10% per year

Time (n) = 2 years

Since the earned profit is reinvested at the same rate, this acts as Compound Interest.

**Formula Used:**

Total Amount (A) = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ

 
 ₹5000 Initial ₹5500 End Year 1 ₹6050 End Year 2 
• +10% 
• +10% Total Value after 2 Years = ₹6050 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 5000 × (1 + 10 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (1 + 1 ÷ 10)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (11 ÷ 10)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (121 ÷ 100)

⇒ A = 50 × 121

⇒ A = 6050

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 6050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Percentage Rate

The effective net percentage change for two successive changes of x% and y% is calculated using the formula: Net Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

Concept of Reinvestment

When profit or interest is reinvested along with the principal to earn further returns, it acts as Compound Interest because you are generating "interest on interest".

SI vs CI Difference

questions.question: A dealer sells a packet of cookies at Rs. 120 after giving a 25% discount on the marked price. If the profit earned is 20%, find the cost price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In this problem, the Selling Price (SP) is given directly as Rs. 120 and the profit is 20%.

The information about the 25% discount on the marked price is extraneous and not required to find the Cost Price (CP).

We can calculate the CP directly using the SP and Profit percentage:

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

CP = (120 × 100) ÷ 120 = 100

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 120

Discount = 25%

Profit = 20%

**Formulas Used:**

MP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

 
 
 CP = ? SP = 120 MP = 160 
 +20% Profit 
 -25% Discount CP × 1.20 = 120 → CP = 100 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, let's determine the Marked Price (MP) for reference:

⇒ MP = (120 × 100) ÷ (100 − 25)

⇒ MP = 12000 ÷ 75 = Rs. 160

⇒ Now, applying the direct ratio formula between CP and MP:

⇒ CP ÷ 160 = (100 − 25) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP ÷ 160 = 75 ÷ 120

⇒ CP ÷ 160 = 5 ÷ 8

⇒ CP = (160 × 5) ÷ 8

⇒ CP = 800 ÷ 8 = 100

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Marked Price (MP) is the price printed on the label. Discount is always calculated on the MP. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Direct CP and MP Relationship

When profit percentage and discount percentage are known, the ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is given directly by: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Extraneous Data in Competitive Exams

In many competitive exams, extra data (like the 25% discount in this problem) is provided to consume your time. Always identify the minimum variables needed to reach the final value before calculating blindly.

questions.question: A wholesaler marks up a batch of 100 identical clocks by 80% on cost and offers a trade discount of 25% to retailers. A retailer purchases all the clocks and spends Rs. 48,000. What is the cost price per clock for the wholesaler?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net profit % = 80 − 25 − (80 × 25) ÷ 100 = 35%

Selling Price (SP) of 1 clock = 48000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 480

Cost Price (CP) × 1.35 = 480 ⇒ CP = 480 ÷ 1.35

CP = 3200 ÷ 9 ≈ Rs. 355.56

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 355.56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total clocks = 100

Total amount paid by retailer = Rs. 48,000

Markup % = 80%

Discount % = 25%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (1 + Markup%/100) × (1 − Discount%/100)

 
 
 
 CP = ? SP = 480 MP 
 Markup: +80% 
 Discount: −25% 
 Net: +35% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP of 1 clock = 48000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 480

⇒ 480 = CP × (1 + 80/100) × (1 − 25/100)

⇒ 480 = CP × 1.80 × 0.75

⇒ 480 = CP × 1.35

⇒ CP = 480 ÷ 1.35

⇒ CP = 48000 ÷ 135

⇒ CP = 3200 ÷ 9 ≈ 355.56

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 355.56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Final Selling Price = MP × (1 − Discount%/100).

Effective Profit %

When a markup% and a discount% are applied, Effective profit % = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discount

When two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given successively, the equivalent net discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

questions.question: IftanA = (3)/(4), then what is the value of sinA?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We are given tanA = 3/4.

In a right-angled triangle, tanA = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

This forms a standard Pythagorean triplet of (3, 4, 5).

Hence, Hypotenuse = √(3² + 4²) = 5.

Therefore, sinA = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse = 3/5.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tanA = 3/4

**Formula Used:**

tanA = Perpendicular ÷ Base

sinA = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

 
 
 A B C Base = 4x Perp = 3x Hyp = 5x 
 

⇒ Let the Perpendicular (BC) = 3x and Base (AB) = 4x

⇒ In right triangle ABC, applying Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ AC² = AB² + BC²

⇒ AC² = (4x)² + (3x)²

⇒ AC² = 16x² + 9x² = 25x²

⇒ AC = √(25x²) = 5x

⇒ Now, sinA = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

⇒ sinA = BC ÷ AC = 3x ÷ 5x = 3/5

**∴ The correct answer is 3/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, the primary trigonometric ratios are defined as: sin A = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, cos A = Base ÷ Hypotenuse, and tan A = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers a, b, and c that satisfy the rule a² + b² = c². Common fundamental triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Fundamental Trigonometric Identity

The most commonly used identity is sin²A + cos²A = 1, which acts as a direct link between the sine and cosine of the exact same angle.

questions.question: If 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ, then what is the value of cosec²60° - cot²60°?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the given trigonometric identity: 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

Rearranging this, we get: cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

This is a universal identity valid for any angle θ.

Putting θ = 60°, the value directly becomes 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation: 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

Expression to find: cosec²60° − cot²60°

**Formula Used:**

Standard trigonometric values for 60°:

⇒ cosec 60° = 2/√3

⇒ cot 60° = 1/√3

**Calculation:**

⇒ cosec²60° − cot²60°

⇒ (2/√3)² − (1/√3)²

⇒ (4/3) − (1/3)

⇒ (4 − 1) / 3

⇒ 3 / 3

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

There are three primary Pythagorean identities in trigonometry:

1) sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

2) sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

3) cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Standard Trigonometric Values for 60°

sin 60° = √3/2 | cos 60° = 1/2 | tan 60° = √3

cosec 60° = 2/√3 | sec 60° = 2 | cot 60° = 1/√3

Area of a Sector (Degree Measure)

Perimeter of a Sector

questions.question: If cos(90° – θ) = x and θ is acute, then what is the value of cos θ in terms of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the complementary angle property, we know that cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Therefore, we are given that sin θ = x.

From the standard trigonometric identity, cos θ = √(1 − sin² θ).

Substituting the value of sin θ directly, we get cos θ = √(1 − x²).

**∴ The correct answer is √(1 − x²).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ cos(90° − θ) = x

**Formula Used:**

⇒ cos(90° − θ) = sin θ

⇒ Base² + Perpendicular² = Hypotenuse²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, we have sin θ = x

⇒ sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse = x ÷ 1

⇒ In right-angled ΔABC, let AB = x and AC = 1

⇒ BC² + AB² = AC²

⇒ BC² + x² = 1

⇒ BC = √(1 − x²)

⇒ Now, cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse = BC ÷ AC

⇒ cos θ = √(1 − x²) ÷ 1 = √(1 − x²)

**∴ The correct answer is √(1 − x²).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

The trigonometric ratios of complementary angles are related such that sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Pythagorean Identities

The fundamental relation linking sine and cosine in any right-angled triangle is sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.

First Quadrant Rule

If θ is strictly an acute angle (0° < θ < 90°), it lies in the first quadrant where all trigonometric ratios are strictly positive, eliminating the need for negative square roots.

Perpendicular from Center to Chord

Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let PT be the tangent to the circle at point T.

⇒ A key property of circles is that the radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

⇒ ∴ ∠OTP = 90°

⇒ In right-angled triangle OTP, applying Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ (OP)² = (OT)² + (PT)²

⇒ (13)² = (5)² + (PT)²

⇒ 169 = 25 + (PT)²

⇒ (PT)² = 169 − 25

⇒ (PT)² = 144

⇒ PT = √144 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

Tangent to a Circle

A tangent is a straight line that touches the circle at exactly one distinct point. The radius intersecting this point of contact is always perpendicular to the tangent line.

Secant-Tangent Theorem

If a tangent segment and a secant segment are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, the square of the tangent length is equal to the product of the secant segment and its external portion: PT² = PA × PB.

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of a DCT between two non-intersecting circles with radii r₁ and r₂ and distance d between their centers is calculated as √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²].

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of a TCT between two circles with radii r₁ and r₂ and a central distance d is given by the formula √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²].
